question.text: What abilities does senior driving demand, and what may eventually be needed?

answer.text: Senior driving demands physical, visual, and mental ability, and the day may come to limit or stop driving temporarily or permanently.

teaching.text: Driving as a senior takes physical, visual and mental ability, and a time may come to limit or stop driving, for a while or for good. Remember: ability now, limits later.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Senior driving demands physical, visual, and mental ability, and the day may come to limit or stop driving temporarily or permanently.

question.text: What are the warning signs of an unsafe driver?

answer.text: Unsafe-driver warning signs run getting lost in familiar places, dents and scrapes on cars and property, and frequent close calls or collisions.

teaching.text: Getting lost in familiar places, new dents and scrapes, and frequent close calls are signs a driver may be unsafe. Remember: lost, dents, close calls.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Unsafe-driver warning signs run getting lost in familiar places, dents and scrapes on cars and property, and frequent close calls or collisions.

question.text: What steps may senior drivers take to limit their driving?

answer.text: Senior drivers may curb night driving with lit routes when necessary, favor light-traffic hours, dodge hard intersections, shorten trips to essentials, skip freeways, and add a right-side mirror.

teaching.text: Seniors can cut night driving, drive at quiet hours, avoid hard intersections, shorten trips, skip freeways and add a right-side mirror. Remember: drive lighter, shorter, safer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Senior drivers may curb night driving with lit routes when necessary, favor light-traffic hours, dodge hard intersections, shorten trips to essentials, skip freeways, and add a right-side mirror.

question.text: Where is the Driver Skills Self-Assessment Questionnaire?

answer.text: The Driver Skills Self-Assessment Questionnaire lives at dmv.ca.gov slash driver-skills.

teaching.text: The Driver Skills Self-Assessment Questionnaire is on the DMV driver skills page. Remember: self-assessment online.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Driver Skills Self-Assessment Questionnaire lives at dmv.ca.gov slash driver-skills.

question.text: How do drivers seventy or older renew, and when are renewal notices mailed?

answer.text: Drivers seventy or older at expiry renew in person with a vision test and possibly other exams, eligible for eLearning knowledge tests when required, with renewal notices mailed about ninety days out and missing notices answered by applications at dmv.ca.gov slash dlservices or offices plus samples at dmv.ca.gov slash driver-ed.

teaching.text: At seventy or older at expiry, you renew in person with a vision test, and notices come about ninety days ahead. Remember: seventy plus renews in person.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers seventy or older at expiry renew in person with a vision test and possibly other exams, eligible for eLearning knowledge tests when required, with renewal notices mailed about ninety days out and missing notices answered by applications at dmv.ca.gov slash dlservices or offices plus samples at dmv.ca.gov slash driver-ed.

question.text: What does the Community Liaison do, and what can it not do?

answer.text: The Community Liaison champions public safety for all Californians with senior and teen focus, mediating fair, lawful, dignified treatment, barred from hearing and reexamination representation yet rich in tools and information.

teaching.text: The Community Liaison works for safe, fair and dignified treatment of all Californians, but cannot represent you at a hearing. Remember: liaison helps, does not represent.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Community Liaison champions public safety for all Californians with senior and teen focus, mediating fair, lawful, dignified treatment, barred from hearing and reexamination representation yet rich in tools and information.

question.text: How do senior fitness, coping, renewal and the liaison fit together?

answer.text: Senior fitness pairs ability demands against limit-or-stop honesty with lostness, damage, and close calls as tripwires, coping pairs seven self-restrictions from night curbs to extra mirrors, self-assessment lives online, seventy-plus renewal pairs in-person vision against eLearning options and ninety-day notices, and the liaison pairs advocacy against no-representation limits.

teaching.text: Ability and warning signs guide when to adjust, seventy-plus drivers renew in person, and the liaison helps without representing anyone. Remember: fitness, coping, renewal, liaison.

question.text: How do you contact Community Liaison and Outreach?

answer.text: Area outreach and liaison contact runs through Community Liaison and Outreach at eight three three, four nine three, zero six seven five.

teaching.text: To reach area outreach or the liaison, call the Community Liaison and Outreach phone line. Remember: one liaison phone line.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Area outreach and liaison contact runs through Community Liaison and Outreach at eight three three, four nine three, zero six seven five.

question.text: What does progressive dementia mean for driving, and who steps in?

answer.text: Progressive dementia ultimately ends safe driving, leaving caregivers, physicians, and law enforcement to halt seniors and arrange other transport, with reexamination details at dmv.ca.gov slash reexamination.

teaching.text: Progressive dementia eventually ends safe driving, and caregivers, physicians or officers may need to stop the driver and arrange rides. Remember: dementia ends safe driving.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Progressive dementia ultimately ends safe driving, leaving caregivers, physicians, and law enforcement to halt seniors and arrange other transport, with reexamination details at dmv.ca.gov slash reexamination.

question.text: What is the Mature Driver Improvement Program?

answer.text: The Mature Driver Improvement Program runs eight hours for drivers fifty-five and older on topics of special mature-driver interest.

teaching.text: The Mature Driver Improvement Program is an eight-hour course for drivers fifty-five and older. Remember: eight hours at fifty-five plus.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Mature Driver Improvement Program runs eight hours for drivers fifty-five and older on topics of special mature-driver interest.

question.text: What can program graduates get, and how long does the certificate last?

answer.text: Insurers may discount program graduates on proof of completion certificates valid three years and renewable through four-hour refresher courses from DMV-approved providers listed at dmv.ca.gov slash seniors.

teaching.text: Program graduates may get insurance discounts; the certificate lasts three years and renews with a four-hour refresher. Remember: three years, renew with four.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Insurers may discount program graduates on proof of completion certificates valid three years and renewable through four-hour refresher courses from DMV-approved providers listed at dmv.ca.gov slash seniors.

question.text: Who qualifies for no-fee ID cards?

answer.text: Drivers sixty-two and older qualify for no-fee Senior ID cards, unsafe drivers of any age may trade licenses for no-fee ID cards good for identification only, and details live at dmv.ca.gov slash id-cards.

teaching.text: At sixty-two or older you qualify for a no-fee Senior ID card, and any unsafe driver may swap a license for a no-fee ID card. Remember: sixty-two plus, no fee.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers sixty-two and older qualify for no-fee Senior ID cards, unsafe drivers of any age may trade licenses for no-fee ID cards good for identification only, and details live at dmv.ca.gov slash id-cards.

teaching.text: One liaison phone line, dementia that ends driving, an eight-hour course at fifty-five, and free IDs at sixty-two. Remember: contact, dementia, program, ID.
